title: Cabinet Pick and Place
summary: A tall wooden cabinet stands ahead of the hovering aerial manipulator, and a small soda can stands inside one of its shelf compartments, behind a closed sliding door. Get the can onto the top of the cabinet: AM-Bench counts success when the can's centre is less than 5 cm above a fixed height just below the cabinet's top surface (there is no horizontal condition) while the can moves slower than 0.1 m/s.
scene: The ground is the world's z = 0 plane; there is no wall. Ahead of the robot stands an immovable cabinet with light-wood panels and metal handles, about 1.2 m wide, 0.6 m deep and 1.68 m tall, its front facing the robot and its top a flat board. From the bottom up: a solid base; a drawer with a horizontal bar handle; a compartment closed by two hinged doors with vertical handles, which are locked; the can's compartment, about 27 cm tall, whose right half (as seen from the robot) is closed by a fixed panel and whose left half is closed by a sliding door with a vertical bar handle; and a top compartment closed by a front panel with a horizontal bar handle. The sliding door slides sideways to the robot's right, in front of the fixed panel, over 0.6 m of travel; it has no spring (it stays where it is left) and its motion is resisted by damping and friction. The bottom drawer and the top front panel are not jointed: they are loose parts held in place only by gravity and contact. The can (4 cm in diameter, 6.4 cm tall, 5 g, with a soda label) stands upright on the floor of the sliding-door compartment, a little in from the front and hidden behind the closed sliding door; its exact spot varies by a few centimetres between instances, and nothing else varies. Nothing moves by itself. The robot starts hovering level and motionless, facing the cabinet, with its arm at its zero joint configuration (end effector a little ahead of and above the airframe) and the gripper closed.
scene_privileged: One environment; its origin is the world origin. Robot at every reset: base_link at (0, 0, 1.0) m with orientation (1, 0, 0, 0) wxyz (body +x is the world +x direction), zero velocity; arm_link1_pitch_joint = arm_link2_pitch_joint = arm_link3_pitch_joint = arm_link4_roll_joint = 0 rad; arm_lfinger_joint = arm_rfinger_joint = 0.001 m (their lower limit: gripper closed, gripper_width 0.002 m). By the robot's URDF kinematics this puts ee_link at about (0.227, 0, 1.124) m with identity orientation and the tool-tip point (ee_link origin + 0.18 m along the ee_link x axis) at about (0.407, 0, 1.124) m; the end-effector command is initialised to the current ee_link pose. Cabinet: cabinet.usd (a MuJoCo-converted asset; panel texture light-wood.png and handle texture metal.png, both local), asset origin at (1.5, 0, 0) m, unrotated. Isaac Lab drives the sub-articulation rooted at pulling_cabinet/pulling_cabinet (fixed to the world; AM-Bench's pulling_door_pos observation is this root, at (2.4, 0, 1.08)); every other part keeps its USD physics. World-frame collision geometry: kinematic carcass of base block x 2.10..2.70, |y| <= 0.60, z 0..0.50, side panels at |y| 0.58..0.60 and back panel x 2.70..2.72, both up to z 1.68; bottom drawer box x 2.10..2.70, |y| <= 0.58, z 0.51..0.79, handle bar reaching x 2.00 (its slide joint has physics:jointEnabled = 0, so it is an unjointed body); middle compartment floor z 0.80..0.82 and two hinged doors (front x 2.10..2.12, handles reaching x 2.00) with hinge limits [0, 0]; the can's compartment: floor z 1.09..1.11, back x 2.68..2.70, ceiling z 1.38, fixed front panel x 2.10..2.12, y -0.57..-0.01, z 1.11..1.37; sliding door (body pulling_door) x 2.07..2.09, y 0.01..0.57, z 1.11..1.37 when closed, its handle a vertical bar x 1.97..1.99, y 0.48..0.50, z 1.14..1.32 on two horizontal standoffs; top compartment floor z 1.38..1.40, front panel x 2.10..2.12, |y| <= 0.58, z 1.405..1.655 (hinge also disabled), handle bar x 2.00..2.02, |y| <= 0.20, z 1.44..1.46; top board z 1.66..1.68 over x 2.12..2.70, |y| <= 0.58, so the top surface is z = 1.68 m. Joint pull_door_slide: prismatic along world +y, limits [-0.6, 0] m, closed at 0 and reset to 0 with zero velocity every episode, so opening moves the door toward world -y (at -0.6 it spans y -0.59..-0.03); Isaac Lab implicit actuator stiffness 0, damping 10, friction 2.0 static and dynamic, effort limit 50. Cabinet masses are not authored (density 0: PhysX derives them from the collision shapes). Can: rigid body can.usd (local, soda.png label), convex-hull collider 0.04 m in diameter and 0.064 m tall, body origin at its centre, mass 0.005 kg, gravity on, no physics material bound. At each reset (mdp.reset_root_state_uniform) its root is set to (2.26 + dx, 0.30 + dy, 1.17) m with dx ~ U(-0.02, 0.02), dy ~ U(-0.05, 0.05) m, identity orientation, zero velocity (AM-Bench's can_pos observation): upright, centre 0.14 to 0.18 m behind the front plane, bottom 2.8 cm above the compartment floor, onto which it drops at the start. Neither the cabinet nor the can is loaded from the web. Scene default physics material: friction 1.0 / 1.0, restitution 0.
success: Success at a control step when both hold: (1) the can's root position (its body origin, the can's centre) satisfies 0 <= z - 1.67 < 0.05 m (drawer_top_z = 1.67 m above the environment origin, which is the world origin; i.e. 1.67 <= z < 1.72 m); (2) the norm of the can's linear velocity is < 0.1 m/s (can_place_velocity_threshold). Nothing else is tested: no horizontal (x, y) condition, no orientation, the can need not be released, and the door's position does not matter. AM-Bench also reports subtask criteria pulling_door_opened (|pull_door_slide - 0| >= 0.2 m), can_lifted (can z > its z at reset + 0.05 m) and can_placed_on_drawer (the success itself); they are informational only. Evaluated after every control step (decimation 1, so after every 1/120 s physics step) on the simulated state; no hold time is required. The episode terminates at the first step where it holds. Otherwise it is truncated by the time limit: episode_length_s = 60 s, i.e. max_episode_length = 7200 control steps; AM-Bench raises the time-out when episode_length_buf >= max_episode_length - 1, i.e. at the 7199th step.
difficulty_note: The can is small (4 cm across, 5 g), enclosed in a shallow compartment behind a closed sliding door, and has to end up still at the height of the top of a tall cabinet, all from a hovering base.
standard_notes: Neither the cabinet's pose, the sliding door's position nor the can's pose is given: the cabinet, the door and its handle have to be found with the forward-looking onboard cameras, the can is hidden behind the closed door at the start, and whether the can ended at the right height and at rest can only be judged from the images together with proprioception. Success is not reported during the episode.
